summary: Streaming response stalls mid-generation after short-lived SDK token refresh
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports SSE/websocket streaming sessions are producing partial output and then silence mid-token when their client-side SDK performs an automatic short-lived access token refresh.

Impact: Several TuneLabs production users experienced truncated assistant messages in their chat UI; sessions stayed open (socket did not close) and did not receive further token chunks until manual page reload. This affected multiple conversations concurrently for a single user.

Environment: TuneLabs uses the Redwood hosted API via our official JS SDK with short-lived tokens (5m TTL) and automatic background refresh. Occurred in us-east production; model redwood/clarity-13b.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use official JS SDK with token TTL set to 5 minutes and auto-refresh enabled.
2) Start a long-form streaming generation (context ~8k, expected stream ~30s).
3) Let the SDK refresh the token in background during the generation window.
4) Observe that the stream emits partial tokens and then stops sending further chunks without closing the socket.

Expected: Stream should continue to deliver tokens to the client uninterrupted or reconnect gracefully; SDK should reconnect if token rotation requires a new connection.

Actual: Stream becomes silent mid-generation. Client socket remains ESTABLISHED (no FIN/RST). No immediately visible 401s on the client; server-side shows an auth check mismatch at chunk-flush that does not trigger connection close.

Temporary workaround: Disable automatic background token refresh for long-running streams (refresh on reconnect) or shorten generative tasks to finish before token rotation. TuneLabs confirmed disabling refresh avoided the symptom for their use case.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 10:22 UTC - Initial triage by CS (Aisha): customer attached browser HAR and SDK logs; SDK shows token refresh event at 00:02:17 into generation.
2026-03-12 11:05 UTC - Engineer (Diego) reproduced locally using SDK with 5m token TTL; observed identical behavior when refresh occurred during streaming long transcript (token arrival at ~12s).

2026-03-12 12:10 UTC - Gateway logs show chunk flush worker attempted to validate active token on subsequent chunk write and returned 401 from auth middleware, but did not tear down connection or surface error to client; message queue for stream remained backed up.

2026-03-12 13:00 UTC - Hypothesis: race between SDK token rotation and gateway per-chunk auth check. Gateway expected either continuous bearer token for session lifetime or explicit reconnect flow; when token rotated mid-stream, auth middleware flagged mismatch and blocked further flushes without closing/hard-failing the connection, causing silent stall.
2026-03-12 14:05 UTC - Further evidence: tcpdump/pcap shows keepalive probes and no application-level CLOSE. No related 5xx from serving-runtime. No memory pressure on serving workers.

comments: Aisha Patel (CS) - 2026-03-12: Customer provided reproducible sample and HAR; marked as P1 due to truncated messages in production.
Diego Morales (Eng) - 2026-03-12: Reproduced locally, collecting gateway + sdk traces. Assigning to gateway/auth owners.

SRE (Maya Li) - 2026-03-12: Verified no worker OOM or eviction; connection kept open at TCP layer. Suspect auth handshake race. Will instrument auth middleware to log token rotation events per stream.
TuneLabs (Customer) - 2026-03-12: Confirmed disabling refresh avoids issue. Can run more tests tomorrow for validation.

Diego Morales (Eng) - 2026-03-13: Hotfix deployed to gateway to treat mid-stream token rotation as signal to gracefully close stream with a structured SSE close event (and reason=auth_rotate) so SDK can reconnect. SDK patch also added explicit reconnect-on-token-rotation for streaming endpoints. Please test.
root_cause: Race condition between short-lived SDK token refresh and gateway per-chunk auth validation. Gateway blocked subsequent chunk flushes when auth middleware received a rotated token but did not close the connection or surface an error to the client, causing silent mid-generation stalls.
resolution: 2026-03-13: Deployed gateway hotfix (PR #1852) to emit a structured close when token rotation is detected mid-stream; deployed SDK patch (PR #312) to proactively reconnect streaming sessions on token refresh. TuneLabs validated in their staging and then production; no further truncated streams observed for their reproducer. Follow-up: add end-to-end test for streaming + token rotation and update docs for SDK token-refresh guidance.
follow_up_actions: Add automated E2E test covering token rotation during long streaming sessions (owner: streaming-team)

Update SDK docs: recommend one of two patterns for long-running streams: a) use long-lived session token for duration of stream, or b) SDK should reconnect and resume on token rotate (owner: sdk-team)
Monitor canary for 48h for similar auth-rotate events across customers (owner: SRE)
Create runbook entry 'streaming-auth-rotation' in Confluence (owner: support)
